scope: Reinspect the manufacturer documents underlying the current cover affordance before further robot-hand substitution or physical opening trials.
observations: The Nicolet guide distinguishes the sliding sample-access door from the hinged compartment cover. Its transmission-standard example loads and unloads through the sliding door.
The brochure photograph shows a raised grip at the sliding-window edge. The inspected photograph and open-cover drawing do not establish the current separate front cylindrical bar.

The current 8 mm diameter, 76 mm long bar and its placement are inferred reconstruction choices, not manufacturer dimensions or CAD. Existing source records already identify handle dimensions as inferred.
The available images do not prove that no hardware revision has a front handle. The finding is insufficient support for the selected affordance, not a categorical absence claim.

The PIKE manual places specimens and a gold reference on the upper sphere port, with a substitution procedure. It does not establish access through this particular reconstructed Nicolet sliding-window geometry.

disposition.next_action: Check source-supported cover-edge and slider-grip access with the installed IntegratIR and the full robot. Keep inferred local dimensions explicit and retain the full installation, measurement, transfer and cleanup scope.
disposition.do_not_infer: Neither the generic transmission sliding-door procedure nor a successful static bar grasp proves that the complete IntegratIR manipulation chain is executable.

search_note: Manufacturer URL fetch through the web reader returned an expired redirect; inspection used the previously downloaded PDF with the exact recorded SHA-256. Searches also found a university mirror of the same manufacturer guide. No reseller claim was used to establish device geometry.
